title: Only the Crafter may touch Spell code and Reviewers may only suggest, with the Crafter barred from reviewing their own Spell
content:
Four constraints combine into a strict separation of duties over Spell code.

**Exclusive authorship**: "Every addition, modification, or removal of code or content within the Spell must be performed by the Crafter" (A.1.10.2.1.11). **Review without write access**: "The Reviewers may not perform any addition, modification or removal of code or content within the Spell, although they may suggest changes to the Spell Crafter" (A.1.10.2.1.12). **No self-review**: "A Crafter cannot serve as a Reviewer for the same Spell," and the team needs "at least two Reviewers... at least one of whom should be a member of a different Ecosystem Actor than the Spell Crafter" (A.1.10.2.1.10). **Mandatory rotation**: "The designated Spell Crafter must be rotated, such that the same person does not craft the Spells for two consecutive Executive Votes" (A.1.10.2.1.11).

Each targets a distinct attack or failure. Exclusive authorship gives every line a single accountable origin — no diffusion of responsibility for how something got in. Read-only review keeps the reviewer adversarial: a reviewer who can edit becomes a co-author and stops being an independent check. Cross-organization review means capturing one Ecosystem Actor is insufficient, since A.1.10.2.2.2.1 shows the concrete rotation (Dewiz crafting is reviewed by one Dewiz and one Sidestream member, and vice versa). Crafter rotation prevents a single person accumulating the position from which a long-running pattern could be introduced across successive Spells.

The combination is why anonymity for Spell teams (A.1.10.1.1) is tolerable: no individual is trusted, so no individual needs to be identified.

The structural exposure is the size of the Roster. A.1.10.2.1.9 names exactly two teams, Sidestream and Dewiz, so cross-organization review has no redundancy — if either becomes unavailable or compromised, the independence property collapses to same-organization review.
description: A.1.10.2.1.10-12 add a cross-organization requirement for at least one Reviewer and rotate the Crafter so nobody crafts two consecutive Executive Votes.
